Re: Urgent Pre-Service Appeal for Hip Arthroscopy (CPT 29914)
Member Name: Taylor Kimura
Member ID: W354999576
Plan: Cigna (Commercial/ACA), State of Kansas
Denial Date: July 31, 2026
Reference Number: POC-37F3AA304D-16940
Treating Surgeon: Dr. Okafor, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To Whom It May Concern,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of the prior authorization request for a hip arthroscopy (CPT code 29914) to be performed by my orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Okafor. The denial letter dated July 31, 2026, states that the submitted documentation was "incomplete" and did not allow a "determination of medical necessity." 

This letter and the attached clinical documentation provide a comprehensive response to the requirements of the Cigna Medical Coverage Policies - Musculoskeletal: CMM-314: Hip Surgery- Arthroscopic and Open Procedures (Effective Date: March 7, 2026). Below, we demonstrate point-by-point how my clinical history, physical examination, conservative treatment, and diagnostic imaging satisfy every medical necessity criterion outlined in CMM-314.

1. Functional Limitations and Symptoms
The CMM-314 policy states that "Symptoms include groin-dominant hip pain that is worsened by flexion (e.g., squatting or prolonged sitting) and that significantly limits activities". 
* My Clinical Record: I have experienced progressive, sharp anterior groin pain on the [affected side: left/right] hip for the past 14 months. This groin-dominant pain is severely exacerbated by flexion activities, including sitting and pivoting. My pain significantly limits my daily living and functional activities; I am completely unable to run or squat, and rest provides no relief.

2. Conservative, Non-Surgical Management
The CMM-314 policy requires a "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical treatment for at least three (3) months".
* My Clinical Record: I have undergone extensive, provider-directed conservative care far exceeding the three-month threshold. I participated in a highly structured, supervised physical therapy program focused on core and hip stabilization along with activity modification for 16 weeks (from February 23, 2026, to June 15, 2026), completing 24 visits. This is fully documented in my physical therapy discharge note. Additionally, I tried oral NSAIDs for 4 months, which failed to provide adequate pain relief.

3. Diagnostic and Therapeutic Intra-Articular Injection
The CMM-314 policy requires "an image-guided intra-articular hip injection with local anesthetic (with or without corticosteroid) to which there was a positive response (i.e., any degree of pain reduction achieved within two (2) weeks after the injection)".
* My Clinical Record: On March 21, 2026, I received an image-guided intra-articular corticosteroid injection on the [affected side: left/right] hip. This injection resulted in a strong, positive response, providing 4 weeks of partial pain relief. This clinical response directly satisfies the requirement of achieving pain reduction within two weeks of the injection.

4. Physical Examination Findings
The CMM-314 policy mandates that "Physical exam demonstrates BOTH of the following findings: ◦ positive anterior impingement sign (i.e., groin-dominant hip pain with forced hip flexion, adduction, and internal rotation) ◦ limited passive hip internal rotation".
* My Clinical Record: Dr. Okafor’s physical examination notes show positive provocative testing on my [affected side: left/right] hip, including a positive anterior impingement sign that reproduces my sharp anterior groin pain during forced hip flexion, adduction, and internal rotation. The physical exam also explicitly documents that my passive hip range of motion, specifically passive hip internal rotation, is severely limited by pain.

5. Imaging and Preservation of Joint Space
The CMM-314 policy requires the "presence of Tönnis Grade 0 - 1 osteoarthritis".
* My Clinical Record: An MRI arthrogram of my [affected side: left/right] hip performed on June 24, 2026, confirmed an anterosuperior labral tear and a cam-type femoroacetabular impingement with an alpha angle of 68 degrees. Crucially, the diagnostic imaging reports that my joint space is fully preserved, confirming a Tönnis Grade 0. This establishes that I have no advanced degenerative joint disease and am an ideal candidate for arthroscopic correction.

6. General Health and Absence of Contraindications
I am a non-smoker, my BMI is 29, and I have no active infections or untreated substance use disorders. 

Conclusion
The clinical evidence enclosed in this appeal packet—comprising Dr. Okafor's clinical notes, the physical therapy discharge summary, the injection report from March 21, 2026, and the MRI arthrogram report from June 24, 2026—proves that my case is complete and fully satisfies the medical necessity criteria of policy CMM-314.

Please reverse this denial and approve the requested hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914) so that I may proceed with this necessary corrective surgery. If you require any additional information, please contact Dr. Okafor's office directly at [Provider Phone Number].

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Taylor Kimura
Member ID: W354999576
